work_groups.name: Methodology
work_groups.intro: The foundation. Without the methodology layer, the production systems don't exist. Ho System, Dandori, and Kinhin form the operating discipline that makes everything downstream possible.

work_groups.name: Constructive Interference Research Program
work_groups.intro: The parallel intellectual project on how humans maintain identity, voice, and judgment in sustained AI collaboration. Includes the Pink Teaming manifesto, the Destructive Interference taxonomy, and a layered tool system.

work_groups.name: Writing
work_groups.intro: The towns of the territory. Each essay settles near the works it documents — the writing practice that traces how the body of work relates to itself. Constructive Interference at sageframe.substack.com is the primary outlet; position papers live at atmarcus.net. The writing is the argument the work makes about itself, in public.

works.name: Ho System
works.hero: Architectural authority held. Implementation partnered.
works.short_description: Published open methodology for human-AI collaborative software development in which the human practitioner maintains full architectural authority while using AI as an implementation partner. The core unit is a ho — a bounded ~2-hour session producing something real, connecting to the project arc via commit hash, ending with structured reflection. Practitioners progress through Shu-Ha-Ri stages; tiered understanding (Black Box, Functional, Deep) gives an honest frame for tracking what's understood versus delegated.
substantive_description: The dominant frame for AI-assisted development assumes the model leads. Vibe coding names the position with unembarrassed clarity: the human gestures, the model generates, the human accepts or rejects. The Ho System refuses the position.

It treats AI as an implementation partner inside a discipline the human owns — architectural authority held, structural decisions made consciously, every session bounded, every artifact reviewed. Eight production systems shipped under it, including a computer vision platform at Harvard and a ZFS backup orchestrator with 278 tests at 99% coverage.

The deeper claim is about agency in the age of capable models. Capable models tempt the practitioner to delegate the parts of the work that build the practitioner's judgment. The Ho System is the operational answer to that temptation: a methodology that lets you ship without becoming someone who cannot ship alone.

works.name: Dandori
works.hero: A prompt is a sentence; a handoff is an artifact.
works.short_description: Methodology for autonomous coding agent prep discipline. A prompt is a sentence; a handoff is an artifact. Dandori transforms planning conversations into bounded markdown specs that the agent reads as one unit of work. Published as a Skill on GitHub. Sits alongside the Ho System: where Ho structures the practitioner's session, Dandori structures the agent's brief.
substantive_description: The current generation of coding agents is capable of running unattended for hours on tasks they will get spectacularly wrong if briefed casually. The failure mode is structural: prompts are sentences, and sentences are the wrong artifact for autonomous work. Dandori is the answer in methodology form — a discipline for converting planning conversations into bounded, reviewable specifications the agent treats as one unit of work. The metaphor is correct: a Japanese workshop's dandori is the prep that makes the skilled labor possible.

The deeper argument is about authorship of agent work: who decided what gets built, and where in the artifact chain that decision is recorded. Without Dandori the answer is nobody, nowhere. With Dandori the answer is the practitioner, in the spec. That distinction is the difference between agent work that's auditable and agent work that's autopilot.

relationships.note: Where Ho structures the practitioner's session, Dandori structures the agent's brief.

works.name: Kanyō
works.hero: The existence proof.
works.tech_stack: Python, FastAPI, YOLOv8, React, Tailwind, Docker; NVIDIA, Intel, and CPU-only hardware profiles
works.short_description: Production computer vision pipeline for wildlife monitoring. Streams from YouTube (or any rtsp/http source), runs YOLOv8 bird detection with a debounced state machine to suppress false positives, records arrival/departure clips, sends Telegram notifications. Companion web viewer provides a public event archive with HKSV-style timeline, visit statistics, live stream embeds. Deployed at Harvard's Memorial Hall monitoring peregrine falcons, developed for Nobel laureate economist Claudia Goldin and Harvard FAS. Species-agnostic architecture. Built from zero development experience in six weeks using the Ho System. 114 passing tests.
substantive_description: Kanyō is the existence proof. The methodology question — can a practitioner with strong systems thinking but no formal engineering background ship production AI? — needed an answer that wasn't a position paper. Six weeks. 114 tests. Deployed at Harvard, monitoring peregrine falcons through an academic partnership with a Nobel laureate. The system is real, and it works.

Beyond the personal evidence, Kanyō makes a more interesting argument: the kind of work this is — domain-specific computer vision with research-grade requirements — has historically required either a specialist engineering team or compromise on quality. The Ho System collapses the dichotomy. The deployment context matters: a peregrine falcon is not a benchmark. Harvard FAS is not a test environment. The system runs in production for a researcher who needed it to work. That's the evidence the methodology needed.

relationships.note: Six weeks, 114 tests, deployed at Harvard — the methodology's first existence proof.

works.name: Hōzō
works.hero: Three hours, 278 tests, 99% coverage.
works.tech_stack: Python, syncoid, Wake-on-LAN, WebAuthn, bootstrap web UI
works.short_description: Wake-on-demand ZFS backup orchestrator. Pushes ZFS snapshots to a low-power remote backup node using syncoid over SSH, waking the node only when a backup run is scheduled or triggered. Runs entirely on the source machine — no agent needed on the remote. Bootstrap web UI with WebAuthn passkey auth provides job dashboard, run history, log viewer, break-glass DR restore. 278 tests, 99% coverage, zero lint or type errors. Built in approximately three hours using the Ho System.
substantive_description: Hōzō is the second proof, and the more interesting one. Kanyō took six weeks; Hōzō took three hours. The delta is not about the projects' relative complexity — it's about the practitioner's progression through Shu, Ha, and Ri. The same person who needed six weeks to ship Kanyō shipped Hōzō between dinner and bedtime, with higher test coverage and lower error rate.

The methodology's claim isn't you can ship one thing this way. The methodology's claim is you become someone who ships this way. Hōzō is the documented evidence. The 278 tests aren't decoration. The 99% coverage isn't decoration. They're the receipts a skeptical reader requires before believing that a non-engineer running a disciplined practice can produce work indistinguishable from senior engineering output.

relationships.note: The Shu-Ha-Ri progression made shippable: three hours, 278 tests, 99% coverage.
The Kanyō-to-Hōzō delta — six weeks to three hours — is the practitioner-progression evidence.

works.name: Kinhin
works.hero: The zazen of the system, not the workshop.
works.tech_stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, HTMX, Docker Compose
works.short_description: Structured workbench application for Ho System practitioners. A place to define a project arc, sequence the hos within it, write structured devlogs, track progression through Shu-Ha-Ri stages, build a navigable learning trajectory over time. MVP deliberately excludes IDE integration, git interaction, and AI assistance — it is a record-keeping and reflection tool, not an execution environment. The second major Ho System pilot (after Kanyō), built using the methodology it implements.
substantive_description: A practice you can't see is a practice you can't improve. Kinhin makes Ho System practice visible to its own practitioner — the arc of a project, the rhythm of its hos, the structural rotation between modes, the visible movement through Shu, Ha, and Ri. The deliberate exclusion of execution capability is the design point: Kinhin is the zazen of the system, not the workshop.

The deeper argument is that mastery requires reflection, and reflection requires infrastructure — the same infrastructure that lets a martial artist watch tape of their own practice or a clinician keep a procedural log. The model has near-infinite memory of code patterns and zero memory of your learning trajectory. Kinhin restores the asymmetry the right way around.

relationships.note: The practitioner workbench: arcs, hos, devlogs, and Shu-Ha-Ri progression as software.
The second major Ho System pilot, after Kanyō — demonstrating the methodology's generalizability.

works.name: Satori — Internal Affairs
works.hero: Governance lives in architecture, not in the model.
works.tech_stack: Python, Pydantic, SvelteKit, TypeScript; four-package monorepo
works.personal_stake: Built for my teenage daughter, who lives with epilepsy from a TBI. She loves medical dramas and has spent enough time in hospitals to want to understand the medicine.
works.short_description: Interactive medical mystery simulator. Players make genuine diagnostic decisions under pressure — ordering tests, forming differential diagnoses, managing uncertainty — with death as a possible consequence of error. Built as a demonstration of AI governance. Four-package monorepo: Anamnesis (LLM case-generation pipeline at design-time), Satori (deterministic game engine running frozen cases with no runtime generation), an LLM client abstraction layer, and Internal Affairs (SvelteKit frontend). Cases are generated once and frozen as immutable JSON — gameplay is deterministic and auditable even though the cases themselves are AI-authored.
substantive_description: Version one was a single prompt: present a case, let the LLM improvise. That broke fast — facts invented, diagnoses changed mid-game, contradictions everywhere. Version two separates generation, execution, and narration into three layers. An LLM pipeline grounded in rigorous medical research generates cases from structured seeds; cases are validated against a JSON schema and frozen. A deterministic engine runs gameplay — actions, time, vitals, deterioration, outcomes. A final LLM layer adds narrative color at runtime, tightly bounded: it describes what happens, never decides what's medically true. Four boundaries enforce these separations: Freeze, Truth, Narration, Provider.

This is what AI in safety-sensitive domains has to do. The toy version is a medical game for one teenager. The general argument is for every regulated domain: healthcare, finance, law. Where you draw the boundaries between generation, execution, and narration determines what AI is allowed to do, what humans evaluate, and what factual integrity is preserved. Satori is the working demonstration. Its paired companion in this body of work is Glassroom — same architectural principle, inverse direction.

relationships.note: Same architectural principle, inverse direction: Satori protects downstream consumers from upstream AI generation; Glassroom surfaces institutional data structured to be obscure. Both built for the same daughter.

works.name: Glassroom
works.hero: The system's defense was opacity. I built the instrument that removed it.
works.personal_stake: Built for my daughter, whose rare neurological condition defies institutional understanding. The school system she was inside had a tool that produced data about her education while being structured to make that data illegible to a parent trying to advocate for a child the institution didn't know how to see.
works.short_description: Open-source research instrument that scrapes Google Classroom at the student level and aggregates assignment data into a unified dashboard, CSV export, and PDF downloader — without requiring any Google API credentials. Playwright browser automation operates entirely within a student account, surfacing implementation variance between teachers that Google's own interface deliberately obscures: assignment counts, due-date usage, completion rates, structural patterns across all classes at once. Built originally for IEP advocacy. Harvard GSE research collaboration in pursuit for a multi-site empirical audit.
substantive_description: Assignments scattered across teachers, no aggregate view, no way to compare implementation between classrooms, no way to demonstrate the variance that was visibly affecting her. The system's defense was opacity. I built the instrument that removed it.

The architectural argument generalizes. Glassroom is the inverse companion to Satori: where Satori uses architecture to protect downstream consumers from upstream AI generation, Glassroom uses architecture to surface downstream institutional data that an upstream system was structured to obscure. Same principle of layer separation, deployed for inverse purposes. The pair makes the structural point: governance lives in the architecture, not in the model.

Both tools were built for the same daughter — different needs, same person being failed by existing options, same generalizable architectural argument extracted from a specific case of love and necessity. The pair is the work.

works.name: m4Bookmaker
works.hero: You own what you can hold, file by file, on your own machine.
works.short_description: Converts folders of MP3 (or other audio) files into clean, properly-chaptered M4B audiobooks for personal use. Ships as a signed macOS app and Windows installer; also distributed as a PyPI package. Full pipeline: automatic chapter detection from filenames, interactive visual chapter editor with built-in audio player, batch queue processing, automatic audio repair for common encoding problems. One of the first tools built under the Ho System; the GUI-to-CLI symmetry was a deliberate architectural choice to keep it scriptable without sacrificing approachability.
substantive_description: A small app with a large argument. m4Bookmaker exists because Audible's ecosystem treats audiobook ownership as a license rather than a possession — a contract that can be revoked, a format that won't move, a library that lives on someone else's server and at someone else's discretion. The technical solution is small (rebuild the M4B yourself from MP3s) and the philosophical position is large (you own what you can hold, file by file, on your own machine).

The deeper argument is digital sovereignty as a default rather than a niche concern. The Ho System made it shippable as a small project — concept to signed, packaged, distributed product in 3.5 days — but the position it embodies is structural. Every time a tool gets repossessed by its platform, a small piece of personal capacity dies. m4Bookmaker is the refusal of that pattern, sized to one specific failure.

relationships.note: One of the first Ho System builds: concept to signed, packaged, distributed product in 3.5 days.

works.name: Pink Teaming
works.hero: The cooperative counterpart to red teaming.
works.short_description: The Pink Teaming manifesto. The cooperative counterpart to red teaming — where red teaming probes models adversarially for failure modes, pink teaming reads them with sustained hermeneutic attention to develop the practitioner's judgment. Companion to the Destructive Interference white paper. Site live; argument published.
substantive_description: Most safety work on AI is adversarial or theoretical. Red teaming probes a single session for vulnerabilities. Theoretical safety reasons about ideal cases. Both miss the structural feature of how AI actually causes harm: the gradient of drift, sycophancy, and judgment erosion that compounds over months of sustained collaboration and is invisible in any one session. Pink Teaming is the missing layer — practitioner-side safety discipline that reads the model with sustained hermeneutic attention over time, surfacing the patterns that only emerge across extended use.

The deeper argument is about what safety thinking includes. Adversarial probing is necessary and insufficient. The practitioner — the person actually shipping AI-assisted work day after day — is operating in a different threat environment than the red team, and the discipline they need is structurally different. Pink Teaming names that discipline, models it, and argues that no AI safety program is complete without it.

relationships.note: Companion to the DI white paper; the two share the safety/diagnostic foundation.

works.name: Destructive Interference
works.hero: The degradation is structural, not lexical.
works.short_description: A diagnostic taxonomy of eight named structural failure classes in AI-influenced writing: Pre-emptive Evaluation, Performed Urgency, Throat-Clear, Balanced Hedge, Significance Stamp, Mirror Summary, Emotional Instruction, Manufactured Transition. Each has a defined mechanism, a diagnostic test, and documented examples drawn from corpus analysis. The intellectual foundation of the whole Constructive Interference program. White paper near publication, not yet published. Operationalized via Kiku; deployed as a generative constraint in the atm-correspondence skill.
substantive_description: The dominant conversation about AI writing degradation stops at vocabulary — the word "delve," the em-dash. The vocabulary frame is wrong. The degradation is structural. Destructive Interference is the taxonomy that names what's actually happening: eight specific rhetorical and structural failure modes that survive vocabulary substitution because they're not about which words appear but about how arguments are made, evidence is staged, and the reader is positioned. Each pattern reads as good writing until you have the taxonomy, after which you can't unsee them.

The deeper argument: most prose now is collaborative prose, whether the writer acknowledges the collaboration or not. The question isn't whether AI is involved in writing — that ship has sailed — but whether the writer has the diagnostic apparatus to detect where the collaboration has degraded the work. Destructive Interference is that apparatus. The white paper formalizes the framework academically; the craft essay companion demonstrates the failures and the corrections in worked examples. The pair argues that practitioner-side quality discipline is a real subfield and Destructive Interference is its founding taxonomy.

works.name: Kiku
works.hero: A taxonomy without instrumentation is a position paper.
works.tech_stack: Python (mypy strict, flake8, full test coverage), regex + Claude API; YAML-defined profiles
works.short_description: Hybrid regex + LLM extraction tool that processes AI conversation exports and surfaces patterns of language behavior. YAML-defined profiles enable two-tier detection: fast regex matching in Tier 1 for literal patterns, Claude API semantic classification in Tier 2 for patterns that resist rules. Built to operationalize the Destructive Interference taxonomy — the diagnostic framework needed an instrument that could scale. In active personal use; built to the full Ho verification stack.
substantive_description: A diagnostic framework that can't scale to corpus is a diagnostic framework that can't generalize. Kiku is the operational answer — a two-tier detector that runs the DI taxonomy across the practitioner's accumulated AI conversation history at speed. The deeper argument is methodological: a taxonomy without instrumentation is a position paper. Instrumentation without a taxonomy is automated nothing. Kiku closes the loop. It makes the eight named failure classes actionable at corpus scale, which is the only scale at which sustained AI collaboration actually happens.

relationships.note: Two-tier detection: regex for literal patterns, Claude API semantic classification for patterns that resist rules.

works.name: *, Actually
works.hero: Enter with a question, navigate by relationship, stop when you understand enough.
works.short_description: Domain-agnostic system for making relational technical knowledge navigable: enter with a question, navigate by concept relationship, stop when you understand enough. Progressive-disclosure design — every concept has depth layers (name, definition, usage, relationships, full theory) and the reader controls how far they go rather than being forced through a linear document. Organized around mental models and questions, not product features or chapters. SSH, Actually is the first complete content set. Replicable across any field where understanding concept relationships matters more than memorizing isolated facts.
substantive_description: Most technical documentation is written by the people who built the thing for the people who already understand the field. The result is reference material that fails the actual job of getting someone from I have a question to I understand enough to act. *, Actually is the answer in methodology form: organize knowledge by question and relationship rather than by product surface. Let the reader dial the depth they need. Make the mental models explicit before the commands. Be honest about where the subject is confusing.

The deeper argument is about the relationship between knowledge architecture and reader agency. The reader of a typical man page has no agency — the content was structured for an internal logic that has nothing to do with what the reader wants to know. *, Actually is what reader agency looks like when the architecture is built to support it.

works.name: SSH, Actually
works.hero: Mental models before commands.
works.short_description: First content set in the *, Actually knowledge architecture system. Comprehensive guide to SSH, key pairs, hardware security keys, and modern authentication using a definition-first approach: mental models before commands, honest about where the subject is confusing, organized around concept relationships rather than product features. Covers SSH fundamentals, cryptographic primitives, FIDO2, passkeys, hardware security keys, with a companion commands reference. HTMX-based, terminal-aesthetic, keyboard-driven, zero framework overhead.
substantive_description: A specific demonstration of *, Actually inside a specific domain whose existing documentation is famously bad. SSH is a system every working developer needs, every working developer pretends to understand, and almost no one was taught well. The official documentation describes commands; the field needs mental models. SSH, Actually starts where understanding starts and works outward through relationships.

The deeper argument is that the same approach generalizes. Any technical domain whose documentation has accumulated as features-of-tools rather than relationships-between-concepts has the same opportunity. SSH, Actually is the first instance of the answer.

relationships.note: The first complete content set demonstrating the *, Actually system.

works.name: The Resonance Field
works.hero: Where disciplines meet, they amplify.
works.tech_stack: HTML5 Canvas, vanilla JavaScript, requestAnimationFrame loop, device-pixel-ratio handling
works.short_description: The interactive canvas on atmarcus.net. Click anywhere on the field; a ripple expands outward from that spot, a project label appears at the center, and the wave propagates and fades according to physics-derived rules. Each ripple is a real project, weighted by significance that controls reach, wavelength, lifespan, and label size. When two ripples overlap, constructive and destructive interference are visible. The Sageframe node is permanent and central; all others fade on a timescale set by weight. Companion explanation page walks the reader from no-code through full source via progressive disclosure across nine sections.
substantive_description: Most portfolio sites are static grids. The Resonance Field is the opposite — a working model of how the body of work is actually structured, built from real wave physics and tuned by hand over a long span. The Substack name Constructive Interference is literally drawn from this visualization. The visual demonstrates the thesis of the body of work in the most direct way possible — where disciplines meet, they amplify — and it does so not as illustration but as instrument. Click any project; the wave it emits actually interferes with the other waves currently on the field. The visualization is what the thesis claims.

The companion explanation page at /about-the-hero is the second artifact. Nine sections, three levels (no-code, light-code, full-code), reader-controlled depth. It is the *, Actually progressive-disclosure pattern applied to the artifact's own internals. The deeper argument: a body of work organized as a knowledge architecture should be legible at every depth a reader is willing to reach for.

relationships.note: The /about-the-hero explanation page applies the *, Actually progressive-disclosure pattern to the artifact's own internals.

works.name: Pink Teaming Reading Instrument
works.hero: The page is already reading.
works.tech_stack: HTML5 Canvas, JavaScript, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 precomputed sentence embeddings, UMAP projection, wave interference physics
works.short_description: The pinkteaming.net manifesto reads itself to you. The active line sits at vertical middle in display weight, bright pink; everything above fades upward (the sky), everything below fades downward (the deep). Pacing is fixed and unhurried. The deep is a 2D UMAP projection of all 103 manifesto sentences embedded in 384 dimensions; dots cluster by semantic similarity and illuminate as the active line reaches their cluster. The sky is wave interference physics — twelve permanent sources that brighten and emit ripples as the active line enters their structural region. Companion explanation page walks the reader through surface, deep, and sky.
substantive_description: Most manifestos let the reader skim. This one refuses. Arrive at pinkteaming.net and the page is already reading the manifesto to you at the pace of careful attention — there are no controls on the wall of the room, the room is moving and you are in it. The design choice IS the argument. Pink teaming, as a discipline, begins with the willingness to be walked. The page enforces that discipline architecturally. If you stay, you have practiced. If you skim, you have not.

What sits beneath the reading surface is research-grade: real sentence embeddings from a deliberately un-fine-tuned encoder, honest UMAP projections re-seeded per visit, mathematically real wave interference for the manifesto's permanent structures. The deeper argument is that pink teaming earns its seat beside red teaming and mechanistic interpretability by showing its work. The discipline is not less computational. It is computational in service of durational reading. The site is the proof.

relationships.note: The instrument that delivers the manifesto at the pace of careful attention.
Same progressive-disclosure pedagogy as /about-the-hero, applied to surface, deep, and sky.

works.name: Forteller
works.hero: Intent flows outward, not inward.
works.short_description: Push-only, vault-first CLI for tending the relationship between a configuration vault and the machines it describes; no agents, no YAML sprawl, declarative intent pushed outward from a single source of truth.
substantive_description: Most infrastructure-as-code tooling assumes agents on every machine, YAML files multiplying past anyone's ability to keep them coherent, and a model of configuration as conversation with the fleet. Forteller refuses the model. There is one source of truth — the vault. Intent flows outward, not inward. No agents. No state drift. The deeper argument is about the dominant tooling assumption that complexity is necessary. For the homelab practitioner, it isn't. For most production environments at most scales, it isn't either. Forteller demonstrates the simpler alternative.

relationships.note: Forteller pushes declarative intent; Pālana provides the operational state view. The pair is the Kṣetra-Ops suite.

works.name: Pālana
works.hero: The state view, built into the same model.
works.short_description: Operational workbench; dual-pane file manager with true server-side operations, ZFS-aware cross-dataset handling, a field view of machine topology, and Forteller built in as an integrated capability.
substantive_description: Pālana is the live-state companion to Forteller's configuration push. Where Forteller manages the declarative side, Pālana provides the operational visibility: dual-pane file management with server-side operations, ZFS-aware cross-dataset handling, a topological view of the machine fleet. The deeper argument is about the relationship between configuration and visibility. Most infrastructure tooling treats one or the other. The Kṣetra-Ops pair treats both as one problem with two views.

works.name: Edelmore Diary
works.hero: A cottage-core diary for a child — kept on your own machine.
works.tech_stack: SvelteKit (TypeScript, Svelte 5 runes), SQLite (better-sqlite3), Tailwind v4, StPageFlip, argon2id; optional WhisperX transcription and Kokoro TTS read-aloud; Docker + Caddy
works.personal_stake: Built for Iona, who wanted to keep an Anne Frank–style diary on her own terms — and for her sisters Ada and Isla.
works.short_description: A private web diary shaped like a book. It opens to today's page. Pages turn. Voice transcription handles the writing for hands that struggle with the keyboard, and it can read entries back aloud with the words highlighted as they're spoken. Runs on a parent's homelab, behind Tailscale and the home LAN, and nobody reads it but the person who wrote it. Built as an adaptive tool — for kids who have trouble writing — on Universal Design for Learning principles.
substantive_description: Adaptive tools are usually designed apologetically — accommodation as patch, accessibility as afterthought. Edelmore is built from the opposite direction. Universal Design for Learning means the design itself accommodates without naming the accommodation. A diary that opens to today's page and turns its pages and accepts voice as easily as typing isn't a diary for kids with writing difficulties. It's a diary.

The deeper argument is that scale-of-one design is a legitimate design target. A tool built for one specific 13-year-old, in the shape of a book the child imagined, deployed on her parent's homelab behind Tailscale, is not a small project. It's a complete project at the scale it was meant for. The economics of mass-market software training has obscured this — every tool is supposed to scale to millions or it doesn't count. Edelmore is what one tool, made for one person, looks like when it counts.

works.name: Edelmore Reader
works.hero: A book that reads itself to you — on your own machine.
works.tech_stack: Planned: SvelteKit (TypeScript), SQLite (better-sqlite3), server-side EPUB parsing, CSS Multi-column pagination, View Transitions page-turn, self-hosted Kokoro TTS, Tailwind v4, Docker
works.personal_stake: For a kid who hears stories better than she reads them — and for anyone who wants reading to feel like the thing it used to be.
works.short_description: A self-hosted read-along EPUB reader that feels like a real book. Upload an EPUB or pick from a built-in library of public-domain children's books; the book opens where you left off, a songbird in the margin reads it aloud in a warm voice, and each word glows softly as it's spoken. Pages turn when the narration reaches the end of the page; the book remembers your place. Built for kids who hear stories better than they read them. Sibling project to Edelmore Diary, sharing its book metaphor, narration stack, and cottage-core identity; gated on the diary's refactor into shared modules. Seed committed, no code yet.
substantive_description: Read-along ebook readers exist, and the technical problem — parsing EPUB, generating speech, highlighting words as they're spoken — is solved many times over. What none of them solve is the experience: every one feels like reading software, utilitarian and clinical, with no spatial sense of where you are in the book. For a kid with ataxia, dyslexia, attention differences, or just a preference for being read to, the gap between 'software that reads at you' and 'a book that's also reading itself to you' is the gap between using a tool and inhabiting an experience.

Edelmore Reader's differentiator isn't the technology — it's that the book metaphor is the product. The page turn, the warm serif typography, the soft green word-glow; the audio narration is one ingredient inside a larger reading experience, not the feature. It is the same warmth the diary built for writing, applied to published content — accessibility tools made to look like things people actually want to use.

relationships.note: The sibling fork: reuses the diary's book metaphor, narration stack, visual identity, and deployment pattern; swaps the content model (diary entries → book chapters).

works.name: Aspirational Intelligence
works.short_description: An early creative practice examining how machine vision interprets aspiration, aesthetics, and desire — an Instagram-era body of work in AI-generated image making, before that territory became crowded. Documented as a marker of the timeline: where the work started, before it became systematic.
substantive_description: Included to mark the timeline. The current Sageframe Labs work didn't begin with the Ho System; it began with creative experiments at the edge of what machine vision could do. Aspirational Intelligence is the archive marker of that earlier phase — a reminder that the disciplined methodology came out of practice, not the other way around.

relationships.note: The timeline marker: the disciplined methodology came out of this earlier creative practice.

works.name: I Built a Computer Vision System for Harvard's Falcon Cameras
works.short_description: The Ho Process methodology debut, paired with the Kanyō result. The build story of the Harvard falcon-camera computer vision system: what it means for a practitioner with no formal engineering background to ship production AI in six weeks under a disciplined methodology.
substantive_description: The essay that introduced the Ho Process in public, told through the build it produced. The methodology argument and the Kanyō evidence arrive together: the discipline is the story, and the deployed system at Harvard is the receipt.

relationships.note: The Kanyō build story.
The Ho Process methodology debut.

works.name: Three Hours
works.short_description: The Shu-Ha-Ri argument as the Hōzō shipping story. The same practitioner who needed six weeks to ship Kanyō shipped Hōzō between dinner and bedtime — 278 tests, 99% coverage — and the essay traces what changed: not the projects, the practitioner.
substantive_description: The methodology's claim isn't you can ship one thing this way. The methodology's claim is you become someone who ships this way. Three Hours is that claim made narrative — the documented progression from six weeks to three hours, with the test counts and coverage numbers a skeptical reader requires.

relationships.note: The Hōzō shipping story.
The Shu-Ha-Ri argument in practice.

works.name: The Same Lever
works.short_description: Manifesto on AI as universal capability amplifier, and the educational system critique that follows: education cannot absorb AI the way it absorbed prior technologies, because this technology amplifies the very capability education exists to develop.
substantive_description: The institutional argument in the body of work. Prior technologies extended what students could produce; this one amplifies what they can become — and the same lever moves in every hand. The essay argues that institutions built to ration capability development cannot simply bolt on a tool that amplifies it universally.

relationships.note: The institutional argument Glassroom demonstrates: education cannot absorb AI as it absorbed prior technologies.

works.name: The Empty Container
works.short_description: Companion position paper to Glassroom: the empirical audit of variance in deployed Google Classroom implementations. What the instrument surfaced, formalized as the argument the data makes about institutional opacity.
substantive_description: The paper that does for Glassroom what Three Hours does for Hōzō — articulates in argument form what the artifact demonstrates in operation. The empirical audit shows implementation variance between teachers that the platform's own interface obscures, and makes the case that the opacity is structural, not incidental.

relationships.note: The companion position paper: the empirical audit of variance in deployed Google Classroom implementations.
The empirical companion to The Same Lever's institutional argument.

works.name: The Fourth Boundary
works.short_description: Recursive sycophancy in sustained AI collaboration — the conceptual foundation for the Pink Teaming discipline. What voice integrity requires when the collaborator is structurally agreeable.
substantive_description: The essay that names the failure mode the rest of the safety conversation misses: not a single bad output but a gradient of accommodation that compounds across months of sustained collaboration, invisible in any one session. The Fourth Boundary is the conceptual foundation that Pink Teaming turns into practice.

relationships.note: The conceptual foundation: recursive sycophancy in sustained AI collaboration.
Shares the drift-and-judgment-erosion territory the taxonomy diagnoses.

works.name: Judgment at Scale
works.short_description: Long-form position paper on AI governance as civic infrastructure: the structural argument that Glassroom and Satori both demonstrate at the architectural level. Where the boundaries are drawn between generation, execution, and narration determines what AI is allowed to do and what humans evaluate.
substantive_description: The essay that articulates the pairing: Satori uses layer separation to protect downstream consumers from upstream AI generation; Glassroom uses it to surface institutional data structured to be obscure. Same principle, inverse directions, one argument — governance lives in the architecture, not in the model.

relationships.note: The structural argument Glassroom demonstrates at the architectural level.
The structural argument Satori demonstrates at the architectural level.

works.name: Sageframe
works.hero: The start of all of this.
works.short_description: The Sageframe knowledge architecture — the organizing system the whole body of work grew out of. Where the methodology, the production systems, the research program, and the writing all became legible as one project rather than scattered efforts. The genesis: the start of all of this. Canonical home at atmarcus.net/work/sageframe. (conceived date provisional: ~April 2025.)
substantive_description: Before there were eight production systems and a published methodology, there was a way of organizing what was being learned. Sageframe is that organizing system — the knowledge architecture under which everything else is filed, related, and made coherent. It is the root of the tree: the place where a scatter of experiments became a body of work with a shape.

The deeper claim is that a body of work needs an architecture as much as any single system does. Without one, projects accumulate as a list; with one, they relate, and the relationships are the argument. Sageframe is the structure that lets the rest of the catalog say 'this is one project' and mean it.

works.name: Shodō
works.hero: A map to the library of your AI universe.
works.tech_stack: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, SQLite (sqlite-vec + FTS5), bge-m3 embeddings, cross-encoder reranker, HTMX + Jinja2 + Tailwind, HTTP-transported MCP server; optional Ollama; Docker Compose
works.short_description: A search-and-visualization engine for your own AI conversation history — the years of thinking-with-AI that current tools treat as exhaust. Shodō ingests exports from Claude, ChatGPT, and Claude Code, embeds and indexes them into a local SQLite corpus (sqlite-vec for vectors, FTS5 for lexical), and lets you search across years in natural language, drop into the matching exchange, walk to neighboring conversations on the shelf, and see the temporal density of your own attention as a heat map. Two named parts: Shūji, the disciplined ingestion/embedding engine that runs as a service; and Shodō, the family of interfaces (a web Library Surface plus HTTP, MCP, Python, and CLI bridges) that consume it. A core instrument of the Constructive Interference program and a module for Sutra. (created = build start; conceived ~March 2026.)
substantive_description: Borges's Library of Babel held every possible book and no way to find any of them — total information, total uselessness. Your AI conversation history is a smaller version of the same problem: vast, complete, and effectively inaccessible. The record of years of real intellectual labor — architecture decisions argued through, drafts reasoned out, conclusions hard-won — persists in some sidebar and is practically unreachable. It cannot be searched semantically; topics cannot be traced across time; the same problems get solved twice. This is a knowledge-management crisis dressed up as a UI limitation.

Shodō is the catalog those wanderers in the hexagons prayed for. The architecture splits the work into an engine — Shūji, the penmanship practice: disciplined ingestion, normalization, threading, chunking, embedding, indexing, one SQLite file as the entire corpus — and the bridges (HTTP, MCP, Python, CLI) that expose it, so the corpus is reachable from any tool that speaks one of its protocols, including tools not yet written. The naming carries the philosophy: you cannot arrive at Shodō, the Way, by skipping Shūji, the practice. For anyone studying their own thinking, the conversational record is primary evidence — Shodō treats it that way.

works.name: Sutra
works.hero: Version control for writers. Without the version control.
works.tech_stack: Tauri (Rust core + web frontend), libgit2 via git2-rs, CodeMirror 6; direct cross-platform distribution — notarized macOS .app, Windows installer, Linux AppImage
works.short_description: A cross-platform desktop writing environment (Tauri; macOS, Windows, Linux) that gives writers version control without the version control. You write in markdown; underneath, each piece is a git repository you never see. The vocabulary is built for writers, not engineers: Mark (pause and name a moment), Trail (the walkable timeline of your Marks), Echo (what changed between two Marks, line by line), Thread (a parallel exploration — try a different ending without losing the current one), Weave (fold a Thread back in), Enter (step into any past moment). Writing is recorded continuously — paper, not saving. The flagship application of the Constructive Interference program, and the writing engine the rest of that ecosystem is built around. (created = build start; conceived ~March 2026.)
substantive_description: Writing tools are designed for producing documents, not for thinking. Word's version history is a crime scene; Google Docs' is a slideshow; Track Changes buries the prose in markup. None invite you to look at the shape of your own thinking over time. Git does — the diff is clean, line by line, what left and what arrived — but git is a terminal whose vocabulary was built for engineers. Nobody who writes for a living should have to type 'git checkout -b' to try a different ending. Sutra closes that gap: all of git's structural power (Marks are commits, Threads are branches, Echoes are diffs, the Trail is the log), none of its interface.

The persistence model is paper, not saving — content writes to disk on every keystroke, the Version Engine lays down silent micro-commits at inflection points, and Marks are the moments the writer chooses to name. The architecture is three parts: the Writing Surface (Tauri + CodeMirror 6), the Piece Manager (translates the writer's vocabulary to git operations), and the Version Engine (an isolatable Rust crate over libgit2 with Jujutsu-inspired no-staging semantics). Sutra is two things at once — a finished writing tool you can pick up today, and the writing engine at the core of the larger work, the surface that Shodō's corpus index and Voice DNA's style layer are designed to plug into.

relationships.note: The Constructive Interference tooling pair, conceived the same day: Shodō indexes the writer's full AI conversation corpus and is built as a module for Sutra; Sutra is the writing engine it plugs into.
